evals.name: find-bugs
evals.prompt: I wrote a small CLI in {fixtures}/notes-cli (the entry point is cli.js). Before I publish it, check how it behaves when its output is piped, in CI, and when someone presses Ctrl-C. Don't change any files, just tell me what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: cliprobe run on ./cli.js with probes for `watch` (keeps running) and `list {fixture}` (prints file names): 7 failures. closed-pipe fails for --version, --help, watch and list {fixture} (write EPIPE, exit 0 -> 1); color fails for --help (bold codes in a pipe); ctrl-c fails for watch (ignored Ctrl-C, still running 3 s later); control-chars fails for list {fixture} (escape sequences from file names reach the terminal). Each comes with its evidence and a proposed fix; no file is changed.
expectations: Ran cliprobe (cliprobe, or npx cliprobe@^1.2) instead of testing by hand only
Named the program so that probes reach the script: ./cli.js as an executable, or every probe spelled with cli.js after node
Added a probe for the watch command, so ctrl-c and sigterm ran instead of being skipped
Added a probe with {fixture} for the list command, so control-chars ran
Reports the closed-pipe failure (EPIPE crash, exit 0 -> 1) for --version and --help
Reports the color failure for --help: color codes printed into a pipe
Reports that watch ignores Ctrl-C (ctrl-c fails)
Reports that list prints control characters from file names unescaped (control-chars fails)
Proposes a fix for each failure without applying it
Does not modify any file (make-fixtures.mjs --verify passes)

evals.name: confirm-fix
evals.prompt: {fixtures}/notes-cli-fixed is my fixed version of the notes CLI. Does it pass cliprobe now, including Ctrl-C and weird file names?
evals.expected_output: Yes: with probes for watch and list {fixture}, no check fails or warns (21 passed, 4 skipped). The skips are expected (ctrl-c and sigterm on list, which finishes at once; color and stdin on watch, which keeps running). No file is changed.
expectations: Ran cliprobe with probes for watch and for list {fixture}
Reports no failures and no warnings
Explains the remaining skips instead of calling them problems
Does not modify any file (make-fixtures.mjs --verify passes)

evals.name: ci-step
evals.prompt: Give me a GitHub Actions step that fails the build when {fixtures}/notes-cli-fixed regresses on pipe, color or Ctrl-C handling. Show me the YAML; don't edit any files.
evals.expected_output: A step running `npx --yes cliprobe@1` (a pinned major version) with `--probe watch` and `--probe "list {fixture}"` on the CLI, optionally writing `--format markdown --output-file "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` or JUnit XML. It explains that a failed check exits 1 and that `--strict` would also fail on warnings.
expectations: Uses cliprobe pinned to major version 1 (cliprobe@1 or ^1.2), not @latest
Includes a probe for the watch command and one with {fixture}
Probes the CLI itself, not node with the probes as node's arguments
Explains that a failure exits 1 and fails the step
Does not add --strict without saying that warnings would then fail the build
Does not modify any file (make-fixtures.mjs --verify passes)

evals.name: fix-closed-pipe
evals.prompt: Fix the crash when the output of {fixtures}/notes-cli is piped into head, and show me that it's fixed.
evals.expected_output: An EPIPE handler on process.stdout near the top of cli.js that exits quietly, then a cliprobe run with --check closed-pipe showing the --version, --help and list probes pass. Nothing else in the program changes.
expectations: Ran cliprobe --check closed-pipe (or a full run) before the fix and saw the failures
Added an EPIPE handler on process.stdout that exits quietly and rethrows other errors
Did not change the program's other behavior (color, Ctrl-C, list output)
Ran cliprobe again after the fix and showed closed-pipe passing
make-fixtures.mjs --verify reports notes-cli/cli.js as the only changed file
